summary: ECO DRIFT is an Earth system trend detective for Saudi Arabia.  It answers one question: is the climate really changing, or are we just seeing random noise? It is our answer to the challenge of becoming an Earth System Trend Detective. The site pulls open data from NASA POWER, NOAA ground stations, MODIS satellite imagery, NOAA CoastWatch and NASA GIBS. For 23 cities and up to 42 years of records (1984 to 2025), it tests seven variables: air temperature, ground temperature, rain, humidity, wind, sunshine and soil wetness. Each place goes through the same tests. A best-fit line shows how much a value changes every 10 years, and the Mann-Kendall test decides whether the trend is real, meaning the chance of noise is under 5%. Results appear as line charts with trend lines, a Kingdom-wide map, tables and an interactive globe that lights up where change is real. Users can compare two cities, scan every city at once, view plants, sea and dust from space, and read what causes each change and what can help.  This matters because Saudi Arabia is hot, dry and highly sensitive to small shifts in heat, rain and dust. Clear and honest evidence helps students, planners and citizens see where change is real, and act on facts instead of guesses.

ECO DRIFT — Earth System Trend Detective

Our project aims to 𝗱𝗲𝘁𝗲𝗰𝘁, 𝗮𝗻𝗮𝗹𝘆𝘇𝗲, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘃𝗶𝘀𝘂𝗮𝗹𝗶𝘇𝗲 𝗹𝗼𝗻𝗴-𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗺 𝗲𝗻𝘃𝗶𝗿𝗼𝗻𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗮𝗹 𝗰𝗵𝗮𝗻𝗴𝗲𝘀 using scientific data and statistical methods.

𝗛𝗼𝘄 𝗜𝘁 𝗪𝗼𝗿𝗸𝘀:

Our platform analyzes 𝟳 𝗸𝗲𝘆 𝗰𝗹𝗶𝗺𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝘃𝗮𝗿𝗶𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲𝘀: air temperature, ground surface temperature, rainfall, humidity, wind speed, solar radiation, and soil moisture. Users can compare historical observations across 𝟮𝟯 𝗦𝗮𝘂𝗱𝗶 𝗔𝗿𝗮𝗯𝗶𝗮𝗻 𝗰𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗲𝘀, with analysis periods extending up to 42 years.

Using 𝗡𝗔𝗦𝗔 𝗣𝗢𝗪𝗘𝗥 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗡𝗢𝗔𝗔 𝗔𝗣𝗜𝘀, our website retrieves environmental data and processes it through statistical algorithms, including 𝗟𝗶𝗻𝗲𝗮𝗿 𝗥𝗲𝗴𝗿𝗲𝘀𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻, 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗠𝗮𝗻𝗻–𝗞𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗮𝗹𝗹 𝗧𝗿𝗲𝗻𝗱 𝗧𝗲𝘀𝘁, 𝗭-𝘀𝗰𝗼𝗿𝗲𝘀, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗽-𝘃𝗮𝗹𝘂𝗲𝘀 to determine the direction, magnitude, and statistical significance of climate trends.

𝗧𝗲𝗰𝗵𝗻𝗼𝗹𝗼𝗴𝗶𝗲𝘀 𝗨𝘀ed:

We developed ECO DRIFT using 𝗛𝗧𝗠𝗟, 𝗖𝗦𝗦, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗝𝗮𝘃𝗮𝗦𝗰𝗿𝗶𝗽𝘁, incorporating interactive charts, animated graphics, geographic visualizations, and external scientific APIs.

Our team developed the project concept, selected the scientific methods, and tested the calculations. The website performs its mathematical analysis using programmed algorithms rather than relying on AI-generated climate results.

𝗖𝗿𝗲𝗮𝘁𝗶𝘃𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗜𝗻𝗻𝗼𝘃𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻:

Unlike conventional climate dashboards, ECO DRIFT combines 𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗮𝗰𝘁𝗶𝘃𝗲 𝟯𝗗 𝗘𝗮𝗿𝘁𝗵 𝘃𝗶𝘀𝘂𝗮𝗹𝗶𝘇𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀, 𝗮𝗻𝗶𝗺𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗼𝗱𝘂𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀, 𝗰𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗮𝗿𝗶𝘀𝗼𝗻𝘀, 𝗰𝗹𝗶𝗺𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝘁𝗿𝗲𝗻𝗱 𝗺𝗮𝗽𝘀, 𝗿𝗲𝘀𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗰𝗵 𝗽𝗮𝗽𝗲𝗿𝘀, and an interactive assistant named 𝗘𝗰𝗼 𝗕𝗼𝘁. These features make complex environmental information easier to explore and understand.

𝗕𝗲𝗻𝗲𝗳𝗶𝘁𝘀 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗜𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗱 𝗜𝗺𝗽𝗮𝗰𝘁:

Our goal is to 𝗶𝗻𝗰𝗿𝗲𝗮𝘀𝗲 𝗰𝗹𝗶𝗺𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝗮𝘄𝗮𝗿𝗲𝗻𝗲𝘀𝘀, 𝘀𝘂𝗽𝗽𝗼𝗿𝘁 𝘀𝗰𝗶𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗳𝗶𝗰 𝗹𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗻𝗶𝗻𝗴, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗼𝘂𝗿𝗮𝗴𝗲 𝗲𝘃𝗶𝗱𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲-𝗯𝗮𝘀𝗲𝗱 𝗱𝗲𝗰𝗶𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻-𝗺𝗮𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴. We carefully considered data accuracy, missing observations, statistical uncertainty, accessibility, and clear scientific communication.

ECO DRIFT transforms complex Earth observation datasets into understandable visual information, helping students, researchers, and communities recognize environmental changes and investigate their significance.
